title: Clasper length analysis
text: Male chondrichthyans undergo rapid elongation calcification claspers mature. Clasper length plotted body length age therefore sigmoid: near-constant juveniles, steeply increasing maturation, asymptotic adults. clasp_length() fits curve: CL=b+(−b)(1+e−log⁡(19)(x−L50)/(L95−L50))−1CL = b + (- b)\left(1 + e^{-\log(19)\,(x - L_{50})/(L_{95} - L_{50})}\right)^{-1} bb aa juvenile adult asymptotes, L50L_{50} L95L_{95} values predictor clasper length reaches 50% 95% way . log⁡(19)\log(19) term makes L50L_{50} L95L_{95} mean exactly — reparameterisation used maturity(), two directly comparable. model fitted log scale nls(). gives multiplicative error, matching way variability clasper length grows clasper size, means fitted curve describes median clasper length given size.

title: Clasper length analysis
text: Females clasper measurement dropped automatically, whole data frame can passed : Claspers around 13 mm juveniles asymptote near 80 mm adults, transition centred 898 mm.

title: Clasper length analysis
text: nls() needs starting values, clasp_length() derives data: asymptotes mean clasper length smallest largest 20% animals, L50L_{50} L95L_{95} interpolating binned means. Fitting uses "port" algorithm asymptotes constrained positive, since negative asymptote make log-scale model undefined. fit fails converge, supply starting values directly:
code: clasp_length(clasp_length, length,   data = spottail, times = 50,   start = list(a = 80, b = 13, L50 = 900, L95 = 990) ) |> summary() #> # A tibble: 1 × 15 #>       a a_lower a_upper     b b_lower b_upper   L50 L50_lower L50_upper   L95 #>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> #> 1  80.2    78.1    81.7  13.1    10.7    15.4  898.      889.      909.  992. #> # ℹ 5 more variables: L95_lower <dbl>, L95_upper <dbl>, Sigma <dbl>, n <int>, #> #   x.range <chr>

title: Fecundity analysis
text: Fecundity chondrichthyans — number utero embryos carried gravid female — typically increases maternal body size. fecundity() fits simplest description relationship, ordinary linear regression: Fi=+b⋅Li+ϵ,ϵ∼N(0,σ2)F_i = + b \cdot L_i + \epsilon, \quad \epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2) FiF_i number embryos carried female ii LiL_i length (age). slope bb increase litter size per unit length, usually quantity interest.

title: Length-weight analysis
text: Length weight perhaps two routinely taken measurements fisheries science, although length far easier one measure. Length can measured quickly commonly standard measurement, especially chondrichthyans. Weight far challenging collect, especially field. needs stable platform , sea, compensating balance accurately measure. Weight also varies gut fullness, body condition, gonad state. case larger chondrichthyan species, often impractical measure adult animals weight hundreds thousands kilograms. reasons, good quality length weight relationships don’t exist many chondrichthyan species precisely information still worth collecting. conversion length weight underpins considerable amount subsequent work quantitative fisheries science. Catch reported managed tonnes whereas biological sampling usually done numbers fish length, moving two requires weight–length relationship, converting population length structure (distribution lengths population) biomass. age-structured population dynamics models commonly used stock assessments need weight--age, normally obtained passing predicted length--age growth curve weight–length relationship; yield-per-recruit, spawning stock biomass demographic calculations follow. relationship underlies body condition indices, compare observed weight individual weight expected length (Froese, 2006). Despite importance, length weight relationship considered trivial, noted Froese (2006) quotes Quantitative Fisheries Stock Assessment (Hilborn Walters, 2001): length–weight analysis “good thing teenage children ” way learning correlation regression, teenager struggles estimating β\beta, one can take comfort assuming β=3\beta = 3. relationship body mass length fishes typically described power curve: Wi=αLiβW_i = \alpha L_i^{\beta} WiW_i LiL_i weight length individual ii, α\alpha β\beta estimated parameters. Individual variability weight also increases length, multiplicative rather additive error structure appropriate: Wi=αLiβeϵ,ϵ∼N(0,σ2)W_i = \alpha L_i^{\beta} e^{\epsilon}, \quad \epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2) Upon log-transformation becomes standard linear regression: ln⁡(Wi)=ln⁡(α)+β⋅ln⁡(Li)+ϵ\ln(W_i) = \ln(\alpha) + \beta \cdot \ln(L_i) + \epsilon ln⁡(α)\ln(\alpha) intercept β\beta slope. model fitted len_weight(), reports α\alpha β\beta b.

title: Length-weight analysis
text: β\beta, exponent, informative two parameters. describes weight scales length: β=3\beta = 3 — isometric growth. Weight rises cube length, body shape specific gravity stay constant animal grows fish doubles length becomes eight times heavier (.e. cube law). β>3\beta > 3 — positive allometry. Large individuals relatively heavier length, gaining girth depth faster length. β<3\beta < 3 — negative allometry. Large individuals relatively slender length. Froese’s (2006) meta-analysis 3929 relationships across 1773 species found median β\beta 3.03, significantly greater 3, slight tendency toward positive allometry norm rather exception. Froese (2006) indicates 2.5<β<3.52.5 < \beta < 3.5 expected range coefficient. α\alpha, coefficient, intercept log scale reflects body form: given β\beta, eel-like elongate species carry smaller values fusiform deep-bodied species. also important note α\alpha depends measurement units length measurement used, changing factor 10β10^{\beta} length converted millimetres centimetres. Values therefore comparable across studies unless units . Froese (2006) provides commonly used conversion factors.

title: Length-weight analysis
text: subtle consequence log-transforming regression weight length back-transforming predictions gives median weight given length, mean. lognormal distribution, mean : E[W∣L]=eμ̂+σ2/2E[W \mid L] = e^{\hat{\mu} + \sigma^2/2} σ2\sigma^2 residual variance. len_weight() accounts — predicted values intervals corrected back-transformation bias, following Beauchamp Olson (1973). size correction eσ2/2e^{\sigma^2/2}, depends residual variance constant across length range. negligible tight relationship grows quickly residual variation substantial: σ=0.1\sigma = 0.1 inflates predictions 0.5%, σ=0.3\sigma = 0.3 4.6%, σ=0.5\sigma = 0.5 13%. Reported values σ\sigma therefore indicate much difference correction makes given data set.
